title.en: Decimal place value and fraction equivalents

text.en: Meera records a length as 2.5 metres. Her friend writes 2.50 metres. They compare the two measurements using the meaning of each digit.

A digit just after the decimal point counts tenths, and the next counts hundredths. A tenth equals ten hundredths. Adding zeros to the end of a decimal part preserves its value. Compare from the highest place to the lowest.
The digit five is in the tenths place, so two point five is two and five tenths.
Regroup the five tenths into fifty hundredths. Both representations describe the same quantity.
A zero hundredths digit does not add any length. The two measurements are equal.
Both numbers have two ones. At the next place, five tenths is greater than zero tenths.

problem.en: Write 3.07 as a sum of a whole number and a fraction. Is it greater than 3.7?

why.en: The first digit to the right is zero tenths and the next is seven hundredths.
Seven hundredths is smaller than seventy hundredths.

requiredIdeas.en: Four tenths and forty hundredths represent the same value.

points.en: Read decimal digits by place value.
Compare the first place where the digits differ.
